title: The Promised Offspring
lead: The Hebrew word zera, "seed" or "offspring," carries one of the Bible's main threads: from the woman's offspring who will strike the snake (Genesis 3:15), through Seth, Noah and Abraham's offspring (Genesis 12:7; 22:18), to David's (2 Samuel 7:12), and in the New Testament to Christ (Galatians 3:16).

sections.b: Zera can mean one child or many descendants, and the Bible uses both senses. Eve names Seth "another offspring" in Abel's place (Genesis 4:25). God promises the land to Abram's offspring (12:7) and that all nations will be blessed through it (22:18), and he promises David an offspring whose throne will last (2 Samuel 7:12–16). The barren mothers of Genesis show that this line depends on God's gift (11:30; 25:21; 29:31). Paul argues that the promise to Abraham's "offspring" (singular) points to Christ, and through him to all who belong to him (Galatians 3:16, 29). Christians have long called Genesis 3:15 the "first gospel." Most medieval Jewish commentators (Rashi, Ibn Ezra, Ramban) read it of the lasting enmity between humans and snakes, while the Palestinian Targums link it to the days of the Messiah.
sections.refs: Genesis 3:15; Genesis 4:25; Genesis 12:7; Genesis 22:17–18; 2 Samuel 7:12–16; Galatians 3:16; Galatians 3:29; Romans 16:20
